metric.why: Announced megawatts are the leading indicator for land, power, and equipment demand. The published numbers come almost entirely from commercial research firms; this site links to who publishes them rather than republishing figures it cannot verify.
metric.definition: Capacity in permitting, planned, or under construction per market, the standard unit for comparing data center booms across regions.

reading.body:
The construction pipeline in megawatts is the leading indicator of data center demand for land, power, and equipment, but its figures come from commercial research firms and cannot be independently verified.

The metric counts capacity that is in permitting, planned, or under construction, broken out by market. Megawatts is the unit that makes markets comparable, because it measures the electrical claim a project makes rather than the number of buildings or their floor area. A region can add many structures and little load, or a few very large ones and a great deal of load, and only the second number tells you what the grid will be asked to carry.

That is why it matters for AI specifically. Compute capacity is downstream of buildings and power, and a pipeline measured in megawatts is a forward claim on both, registered at the permitting and planning stage, before steel goes up and long before any workload runs. It is the earliest public signal that demand is being booked into a region, and it moves ahead of the equipment orders and interconnection requests that follow.

What it does not tell you is how much of that capacity will actually be built. The pipeline mixes stages from permitting through active construction, and it carries no schedule, no completion rate, and no confirmation that the power to serve it will be available. No market-level figures appear in this data, so no ranking or trend can be read from it directly. The numbers are compiled almost entirely by commercial research firms, which is a different kind of source than a grid operator or a regulator, and they should be read as developer intent rather than as verified load.
